title: Lifting a proper clopen fibre part over a henselian pair
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a separated finite-type morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $X_0=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. If $Z\subseteq X_0$ is an open and closed subspace and $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is proper, then there is an open and closed subspace $W\subseteq X$, proper over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)=Z$ as subspaces of $X_0$. An open subspace has the structure sheaf restricted from the ambient algebraic space.

source.place: Tag 0CWI, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian. The scheme version is more-morphisms.tex Tag 0CT9; that scheme version alone does not give the assertion for spaces.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, and denote base change to $S_0$ by a subscript $0$. By [lem-sfb-space-weak-chow] choose a universally surjective proper map $\varphi:X\prime\to X$ from a quasi-compact separated scheme admitting an immersion into a finite projective space over $S$. Properness gives separatedness and finite type for $\varphi$ by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Thus $X\prime\to S$ is separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] and finite type by [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-composition]. The chart convention agrees with scheme local finite type by [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]; quasi-compactness here is already supplied by weak Chow. These are exactly the hypotheses on the scheme required below.

Put $Z\prime=X\prime_0\times_{X_0}Z$. Since $Z$ is open and closed, this is the open and closed subscheme of $X\prime_0$ on its inverse image: on every scheme test this is an open subscheme, and the complementary open pulls back to its complement [def-a1-space-open-subspace, lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The morphism $Z\prime\to Z$ is the base change of $\varphi$, so it is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. Since $Z\to S_0$ is proper, [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition] makes $Z\prime\to S_0$ proper. By Step 1, $X\prime\to S$ is a separated finite-type morphism of schemes, and $Z\prime\to S_0$ is proper as a morphism of schemes [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-henselian-proper-clopen-lift] to $X\prime$ and $Z\prime$ over the same pair $(A,I)$, obtaining a clopen subscheme $W\prime\subseteq X\prime$, proper over $S$, with $W\prime_0=Z\prime$ as subschemes.

Let $Q_1=|\varphi|(|W\prime|)$ and $Q_2=|\varphi|(|X\prime\setminus W\prime|)$. Both are closed because $\varphi$ is proper, hence its point map is closed [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Their union is $|X|$ by surjectivity. Let $D=|W\prime|\cap|\varphi|^{-1}(Q_2)$; continuity from [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] makes $D$ closed in $|W\prime|$. Its image $C$ in $|S|$ is closed because $W\prime\to S$ is proper. Set-theoretically $C$ is precisely the image of $Q_1\cap Q_2$ in $S$: a point of the intersection has a lift in $W\prime$, and that lift belongs to $D$. This obtains the closed image needed in 0CWI without choosing a closed structure on $Q_1$.

If $Q_1\cap Q_2$ were nonempty, its image $C$ would contain a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$. Since $C$ is closed, it contains $V(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-prime-connected], $V(\mathfrak p+I)$ is nonempty; hence $C$ meets $|S_0|$. Choose $x\in Q_1\cap Q_2$ above such a point. The fibre-product point-image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] shows that $x$ is in the closed fibre and has lifts there both from $W\prime_0$ and from $(X\prime\setminus W\prime)_0$. Both lifts map to the same point of $|X_0|$: the map $|X_0|\to|X|$ is injective, because $X_0\to X$ is a monomorphism of sheaves (a base change of the monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to S$), so two field-valued points of $X_0$ whose images in $X$ agree after a common field extension already agree there [def-a1-space-point-topology]. The first lift maps to $Z$, since $W\prime_0=\varphi_0^{-1}(Z)$, whereas the second maps to its complementary open in $X_0$. These opens are disjoint, a contradiction. Thus $Q_1\cap Q_2=\varnothing$ and $Q_1=|X|\setminus Q_2$ is clopen.

To realize $Q_1$ as an open subspace, choose a scheme atlas $p:U\to X$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space] and put $O=p^{-1}(Q_1)\subseteq U$. This is an open subscheme by continuity [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. For $R=U\times_XU$ the two inverse images of $O$ agree: both are the inverse image of $Q_1$ under the same composite $R\to X$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-open-chart-morphism-descent] to the map $O\to X$ induced by $p$; its two restrictions agree. It supplies an open subspace $W\subseteq X$ with $U\times_XW=O$. Surjectivity of the atlas and the point-image formula identify $|W|$ with $Q_1$. The complement is also open. On any scheme test $T\to X$, $W_T$ is the corresponding clopen open subscheme; its inclusion is a closed immersion because the structure-sheaf map is the identity on $W_T$ and maps to zero on its open complement. Thus $W\to X$ is a closed immersion by the scheme-test definition [def-weil-closed-immersion].

The equalities $\varphi^{-1}(Q_1)=|W\prime|$ and $\varphi^{-1}(Q_2)=|X\prime\setminus W\prime|$ follow from disjointness and surjectivity. Equality of open subspaces is detected on point images by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]; hence $\varphi^{-1}(W)=W\prime$ and $W\prime\to W$ is surjective, and remains so after every base change by that same point-image formula. For any algebraic space $T\to S$ and closed subset $F\subseteq|W\times_ST|$, its inverse image in $|W\prime\times_ST|$ is closed by continuity. The latter space is proper over $T$ by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change], so its image in $|T|$ is closed. Surjectivity identifies this image with the image of $F$. Thus $W\to S$ is universally closed. Its inclusion into $X$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], hence separated and finite type. Compose with $X\to S$: [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] gives separatedness and [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-composition] gives finite type. Therefore $W\to S$ is proper by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

Finally, base changing the surjection $\varphi$ gives a surjection $\varphi_0$; this follows either from its stated universal surjectivity or from the point-image formula. The inverse images of the two open subspaces $W_0,Z\subseteq X_0$ along $\varphi_0$ are both $W\prime_0=Z\prime$. Surjectivity gives equality of their point images, and [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives equality of the open subfunctors. Since open subspaces carry the restricted structure sheaf, this is $W_0=Z$ as subspaces, as required.

lean.statement: theorem exists_proper_clopen_lift_of_henselianPair {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I] (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))))) (hsep : MapIsSeparated f) (hft : MapIsFiniteType f) (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))) (i : Z ⟶ enlargedFibreProduct (henselianPairClosedFibreBaseMap I) f) (hopen : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom) (hclosed : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom) (hproper : MapIsProper (i ≫ enlargedFibreProductFst (henselianPairClosedFibreBaseMap I) f)) : ∃ (W : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))) (w : W ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) w.hom.hom ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) w.hom.hom ∧ MapIsProper (w ≫ f) ∧ ∃ l : Z ⟶ W, IsPullback l i w (henselianPairClosedFibreInclusion I f)
